ir.intuition: Reference builder: all winner/loser pairs by objective ordering.

ir.name: builder_gap_topk_pairs_003
ir.intuition: Constructs pairwise preferences by ranking candidates with lower objective as winners, then keeping only the largest objective gaps per batch item to focus learning on clearly better-vs-worse comparisons while capping total pairs.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    # objective: [B, N], lower is better
    B, N = objective.shape

    gap_thr = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.05))
    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 128))
    per_batch_cap = int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_batch', 8))

    # Pairwise gap matrix: positive means i is better (lower objective) than j
    gap = objective[:, None, :] - objective[:, :, None]  # [B, N, N] == obj[j]-obj[i]

    # Valid directed pairs i->j where i wins over j by at least gap_thr
    valid = gap > gap_thr
    # Exclude diagonal explicitly
    valid = valid & (~torch.eye(N, dtype=torch.bool, device=objective.device)[None, :, :])

    # Score pairs by gap size; invalid pairs get -inf so they won't be selected
    neg_inf = torch.full((), float('-inf'), device=objective.device)
    score = torch.where(valid, gap, neg_inf)  # [B, N, N]

    # Select up to per_batch_cap pairs per batch item using topk over flattened pairs
    K = per_batch_cap
    if K > N * N:
        K = N * N
    flat_score = score.reshape(B, N * N)
    topk_val, topk_idx = flat_score.topk(K, dim=1)
    keep = topk_val > neg_inf

    b_idx = torch.arange(B, device=objective.device)[:, None].expand(B, K)[keep]
    flat_idx = topk_idx[keep]
    winner_idx = (flat_idx // N)
    loser_idx = (flat_idx % N)

    # Global cap (slice; no randomness)
    if b_idx.numel() > max_pairs:
        b_idx = b_idx[:max_pairs]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[:max_pairs]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[:max_pairs]

    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx),
        weight=None,
        meta={
            'builder': 'gap_topk_pairs',
            'gap_threshold': gap_thr,
            'max_pairs': max_pairs,
            'max_pairs_per_batch': per_batch_cap,
        },
    )

ir.name: builder_anchor_gap_topk_001
ir.intuition: Build stable preferences by comparing each candidate to per-instance anchors (best/worst objective) and only keeping sufficiently separated (objective-gap) pairs, then cap the global pair count with deterministic top-k by gap to respect the pairing budget.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']  # [B, N], lower is better
    B, N = objective.shape

    # Anchors per instance
    best_idx = objective.argmin(dim=1)  # [B]
    worst_idx = objective.argmax(dim=1)  # [B]

    thr = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))

    # Candidate indices
    j = torch.arange(N, device=objective.device)  # [N]

    # Pair type 1: best beats others if objective gap is large enough
    best_obj = objective.gather(1, best_idx[:, None])  # [B,1]
    diff_best = objective - best_obj  # [B,N]
    mask_best = diff_best > thr
    mask_best = mask_best & (j[None, :] != best_idx[:, None])

    b1, l1 = mask_best.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    w1 = best_idx[b1]
    gap1 = diff_best[b1, l1]

    # Pair type 2: others beat worst if objective gap is large enough
    worst_obj = objective.gather(1, worst_idx[:, None])  # [B,1]
    diff_worst = worst_obj - objective  # [B,N]
    mask_worst = diff_worst > thr
    mask_worst = mask_worst & (j[None, :] != worst_idx[:, None])

    b2, w2 = mask_worst.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    l2 = worst_idx[b2]
    gap2 = diff_worst[b2, w2]

    # Concatenate pairs
    b_idx = torch.cat([b1, b2], dim=0)
    winner_idx = torch.cat([w1, w2], dim=0)
    loser_idx = torch.cat([l1, l2], dim=0)
    gap = torch.cat([gap1, gap2], dim=0)

    # If no pairs, return empty PrefBatch
    if b_idx.numel() == 0:
        empty = objective.new_empty((0,), dtype=torch.long)
        return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(empty, empty, empty), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'anchor_gap_topk', 'thr': thr, 'max_pairs': int(extra.get('max_pairs', 128))})

    # Deterministic global cap by largest objective-gap (most confident)
    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 128))
    if b_idx.numel() > max_pairs:
        k = max_pairs
        _, topi = torch.topk(gap, k=k, largest=True, sorted=False)
        b_idx = b_idx[topi]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[topi]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[topi]

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'anchor_gap_topk', 'thr': thr, 'max_pairs': max_pairs})

ir.name: builder_sampled_pairs_gapweight_001
ir.intuition: Keep sampled winner/loser pairs but add a nonnegative weight proportional to the objective gap so clearer improvements contribute more signal while near-ties contribute less noise.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    # Pairs where winner has lower objective (lower is better)
    mask = objective[:, :, None] < objective[:, None, :]
    b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx = mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)

    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 452))
    if b_idx.numel() > max_pairs:
        perm = torch.randperm(b_idx.numel(), device=b_idx.device)[:max_pairs]
        b_idx = b_idx[perm]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[perm]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[perm]

    # Nonnegative weighting by objective gap; optional threshold to drop near-ties
    gap = (objective[b_idx, loser_idx] - objective[b_idx, winner_idx]).clamp_min(0)
    gap_threshold = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))
    if gap_threshold > 0.0:
        keep = gap >= gap_threshold
        b_idx = b_idx[keep]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[keep]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[keep]
        gap = gap[keep]

    weight = gap
    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=weight, meta={'builder': 'sampled_pairs_gapweight', 'max_pairs': max_pairs, 'gap_threshold': gap_threshold})

ir.name: builder_gap_threshold_pairs_001
ir.intuition: Filter pairwise preferences to only include comparisons with a minimum objective gap (configurable), reducing ambiguous near-ties and improving signal-to-noise for training generalization.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    # lower objective is better
    gap_threshold = extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0)

    # For each (winner, loser), require winner strictly better AND gap >= threshold
    # gap = obj_loser - obj_winner
    gap = objective[:, None, :] - objective[:, :, None]
    mask = gap > gap_threshold

    b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx = mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx),
        weight=None,
        meta={'builder': 'gap_threshold_pairs', 'gap_threshold': float(gap_threshold)}
    )

ir.name: rank_stratified_cover_v1
ir.intuition: Parents rely on objective-based winner/loser masks (strength: correct direction, simple, vectorized) but either explode to all pairs or cap via randomness/flat thresholds (weakness: poor per-instance coverage control and budget inefficiency). This builder keeps objective-consistent ordering but switches to rank-stratified, deterministic pair generation: each instance contributes pairs from near-best, mid, and tail ranks with a per-instance cap to ensure broad coverage under a fixed budget.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    # lower objective is better
    B, N = objective.shape

    # Sort to ranks (ascending objective). ranks[b, r] = original index at rank r.
    ranks = objective.argsort(dim=1)

    # Per-instance budget and stratification.
    max_pairs_per_instance = int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_instance', 6))
    max_pairs_per_instance = max(1, max_pairs_per_instance)

    # Allocate (roughly) 3 strata: near-best, mid, tail.
    k1 = max(1, max_pairs_per_instance // 3)
    k2 = max(1, max_pairs_per_instance // 3)
    k3 = max_pairs_per_instance - k1 - k2
    if k3 < 0:
        k3 = 0

    # Helper indices (vectorized). Use clamped ranges to avoid empty when N small.
    device = objective.device

    # Near-best: top ranks vs a window of later ranks.
    t = min(k1, N)
    w = min(max(1, int(extra.get('near_window', 3))), max(1, N - 1))
    i1 = torch.arange(t, device=device)
    j1 = (i1[:, None] + torch.arange(1, w + 1, device=device)[None, :]).clamp(max=N - 1)

    # Mid: center ranks vs offset ahead.
    t2 = min(k2, N)
    mid_center = (N - 1) // 2
    half = t2 // 2
    i2 = (mid_center + torch.arange(t2, device=device) - half).clamp(min=0, max=N - 2)
    step2 = max(1, int(extra.get('mid_step', 2)))
    j2 = (i2 + step2).clamp(max=N - 1)

    # Tail: compare a few worst ranks against best rank.
    t3 = min(k3, N)
    i3 = (N - 1 - torch.arange(t3, device=device)).clamp(min=1, max=N - 1)
    j3 = torch.zeros((t3,), device=device, dtype=i3.dtype)

    # Build pairs in rank-space, then map to original indices.
    # 1) near-best pairs: i1 (better rank) beats j1 (worse rank)
    if t > 0:
        win1 = ranks[:, i1]  # [B, t]
        lose1 = ranks[:, j1]  # [B, t, w]
        win1 = win1[:, :, None].expand_as(lose1)
        b1 = torch.arange(B, device=device)[:, None, None].expand_as(lose1)
        b1 = b1.reshape(-1)
        win1 = win1.reshape(-1)
        lose1 = lose1.reshape(-1)
    else:
        b1 = ranks.new_empty((0,), dtype=torch.long)
        win1 = ranks.new_empty((0,), dtype=torch.long)
        lose1 = ranks.new_empty((0,), dtype=torch.long)

    # 2) mid pairs: i2 beats j2
    if t2 > 0:
        win2 = ranks[:, i2]
        lose2 = ranks[:, j2]
        b2 = torch.arange(B, device=device)[:, None].expand_as(win2).reshape(-1)
        win2 = win2.reshape(-1)
        lose2 = lose2.reshape(-1)
    else:
        b2 = ranks.new_empty((0,), dtype=torch.long)
        win2 = ranks.new_empty((0,), dtype=torch.long)
        lose2 = ranks.new_empty((0,), dtype=torch.long)

    # 3) tail pairs: best beats i3 (worst-ish)
    if t3 > 0:
        win3 = ranks[:, j3]
        lose3 = ranks[:, i3]
        b3 = torch.arange(B, device=device)[:, None].expand_as(win3).reshape(-1)
        win3 = win3.reshape(-1)
        lose3 = lose3.reshape(-1)
    else:
        b3 = ranks.new_empty((0,), dtype=torch.long)
        win3 = ranks.new_empty((0,), dtype=torch.long)
        lose3 = ranks.new_empty((0,), dtype=torch.long)

    b_idx = torch.cat([b1, b2, b3], dim=0)
    winner_idx = torch.cat([win1, win2, win3], dim=0)
    loser_idx = torch.cat([lose1, lose2, lose3], dim=0)

    # Remove accidental self-pairs (can happen when N small / clamping).
    keep = winner_idx != loser_idx
    b_idx = b_idx[keep]
    winner_idx = winner_idx[keep]
    loser_idx = loser_idx[keep]

    # Global cap without randomness: keep earliest pairs.
    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 0))
    if max_pairs and b_idx.numel() > max_pairs:
        b_idx = b_idx[:max_pairs]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[:max_pairs]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[:max_pairs]

    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx),
        weight=None,
        meta={
            'builder': 'rank_stratified_cover',
            'max_pairs_per_instance': max_pairs_per_instance,
            'near_window': int(extra.get('near_window', 3)),
            'mid_step': int(extra.get('mid_step', 2)),
            'max_pairs': max_pairs
        }
    )

ir.name: anchor_gap_topk_001
ir.intuition: Prefer clear improvements by pairing each instance's best (lowest objective) candidate against its worst/most-different candidates, filtering by a minimum objective gap and capping total pairs via top-k anchors for stable, budgeted supervision.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']  # [B, N]
    B, N = objective.shape

    # Anchors: best (min) and worst (max) per instance
    best_idx = objective.argmin(dim=1)  # [B]
    worst_idx = objective.argmax(dim=1)  # [B]

    # Objective gaps relative to anchors (positive means anchor is better)
    obj_best = objective.gather(1, best_idx[:, None])  # [B,1]
    gap_vs_best = objective - obj_best  # [B,N]

    obj_worst = objective.gather(1, worst_idx[:, None])  # [B,1]
    gap_worst_vs = obj_worst - objective  # [B,N]

    thr = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))
    k = int(extra.get('k', 4))
    k = max(1, min(k, N))

    # Best beats others with sufficient gap
    elig_best = gap_vs_best > thr  # [B,N]
    gap_for_topk = gap_vs_best.masked_fill(~elig_best, float('-inf'))
    topk_best_vals, topk_best_idx = torch.topk(gap_for_topk, k=k, dim=1)
    valid_best = topk_best_vals.isfinite()

    # Others beat worst with sufficient gap (worst is loser)
    elig_worst = gap_worst_vs > thr  # [B,N]
    gap_for_topk2 = gap_worst_vs.masked_fill(~elig_worst, float('-inf'))
    topk_worst_vals, topk_worst_winner_idx = torch.topk(gap_for_topk2, k=k, dim=1)
    valid_worst = topk_worst_vals.isfinite()

    # Flatten pairs
    b_arange = torch.arange(B, device=objective.device)
    b_rep = b_arange[:, None].expand(B, k)

    b1 = b_rep[valid_best]
    w1 = best_idx[:, None].expand(B, k)[valid_best]
    l1 = topk_best_idx[valid_best]

    b2 = b_rep[valid_worst]
    w2 = topk_worst_winner_idx[valid_worst]
    l2 = worst_idx[:, None].expand(B, k)[valid_worst]

    b_idx = torch.cat([b1, b2], dim=0)
    winner_idx = torch.cat([w1, w2], dim=0)
    loser_idx = torch.cat([l1, l2], dim=0)

    # Remove any accidental self-pairs
    keep = winner_idx != loser_idx
    b_idx = b_idx[keep]
    winner_idx = winner_idx[keep]
    loser_idx = loser_idx[keep]

    # Budget cap without randomness: keep largest objective gaps
    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 128))
    max_pairs = max(1, max_pairs)
    if b_idx.numel() > max_pairs:
        gaps = (objective[b_idx, loser_idx] - objective[b_idx, winner_idx]).abs()
        _, sel = torch.topk(gaps, k=max_pairs, largest=True)
        b_idx = b_idx[sel]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[sel]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[sel]

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'anchor_gap_topk', 'gap_threshold': thr, 'k': k, 'max_pairs': max_pairs})

ir.name: rank_strat_cap_v1
ir.intuition: Builds preferences by ranking candidates per instance (lower objective is better) and pairing within stratified rank bands (near-best vs mid, mid vs tail, best vs tail) to ensure coverage while capping pairs per instance without random sampling.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    # Rank-based, stratified pairing with per-instance cap; no randomness.
    B, K = objective.shape
    device = objective.device

    # Sort ascending: rank 0 is best (lowest objective).
    sorted_obj, sorted_idx = objective.sort(dim=1, descending=False)

    # Choose band sizes deterministically from K.
    top_n = int(extra.get('top_n', max(1, K // 4)))
    mid_n = int(extra.get('mid_n', max(1, K // 2)))
    tail_n = int(extra.get('tail_n', max(1, K - top_n - mid_n)))

    top_n = max(1, min(top_n, K))
    mid_n = max(1, min(mid_n, K - top_n))
    tail_n = max(1, min(tail_n, K - top_n - mid_n))

    top_idx = sorted_idx[:, :top_n]
    mid_idx = sorted_idx[:, top_n:top_n + mid_n]
    tail_idx = sorted_idx[:, top_n + mid_n:top_n + mid_n + tail_n]

    # Helper: make all cross pairs A (winners) vs B (losers) in a vectorized way.
    def _cross_pairs(w_idx, l_idx):
        # w_idx: [B, W], l_idx: [B, L]
        W = w_idx.shape[1]
        L = l_idx.shape[1]
        b = torch.arange(B, device=device)[:, None, None].expand(B, W, L).reshape(-1)
        w = w_idx[:, :, None].expand(B, W, L).reshape(-1)
        l = l_idx[:, None, :].expand(B, W, L).reshape(-1)
        return b, w, l

    b1, w1, l1 = _cross_pairs(top_idx, mid_idx)   # near-best vs mid
    b2, w2, l2 = _cross_pairs(mid_idx, tail_idx)  # mid vs tail
    b3, w3, l3 = _cross_pairs(top_idx, tail_idx)  # best vs tail (strong signal)

    b_all = torch.cat([b1, b2, b3], dim=0)
    w_all = torch.cat([w1, w2, w3], dim=0)
    l_all = torch.cat([l1, l2, l3], dim=0)

    # Enforce correctness using objective (handles ties / band edge cases).
    ow = objective[b_all, w_all]
    ol = objective[b_all, l_all]
    keep = ow < ol
    b_all = b_all[keep]
    w_all = w_all[keep]
    l_all = l_all[keep]

    # Per-instance cap: keep the strongest margins per instance deterministically.
    per_instance_cap = int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_instance', 2))
    per_instance_cap = max(1, per_instance_cap)

    # Score = margin (loser - winner); larger is better.
    margin = (objective[b_all, l_all] - objective[b_all, w_all])

    # Build a [B, Pmax] table by sorting within each instance using a stable global key.
    # We sort by (b_idx, -margin) via a composite key.
    # Normalize margin to avoid dependence on absolute scale in the composite key.
    m = margin
    m_min = m.min()
    m_max = m.max()
    denom = (m_max - m_min).clamp_min(1e-12)
    m_norm = (m - m_min) / denom  # in [0,1]
    key = b_all.to(m_norm.dtype) + (1.0 - m_norm)  # smaller key => larger margin within same b
    order = key.argsort(stable=True)

    b_s = b_all[order]
    w_s = w_all[order]
    l_s = l_all[order]

    # Compute rank position within each instance in the sorted list.
    # First, count pairs per instance.
    counts = torch.bincount(b_s, minlength=B)
    max_len = int(counts.max().item()) if counts.numel() > 0 else 0
    if max_len == 0:
        return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_s, w_s, l_s), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'rank_strat_cap', 'top_n': top_n, 'mid_n': mid_n, 'tail_n': tail_n, 'max_pairs_per_instance': per_instance_cap})

    # Create positions 0..count-1 for each group without Python loops.
    # Build a mask matrix [B, max_len] where True indicates a valid slot.
    slots = torch.arange(max_len, device=device)[None, :].expand(B, max_len)
    valid = slots < counts[:, None]
    pos = slots[valid]  # positions aligned with b_s order

    # Keep first per_instance_cap positions per instance.
    keep2 = pos < per_instance_cap
    b_out = b_s[keep2]
    w_out = w_s[keep2]
    l_out = l_s[keep2]

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_out, w_out, l_out), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'rank_strat_cap', 'top_n': top_n, 'mid_n': mid_n, 'tail_n': tail_n, 'max_pairs_per_instance': per_instance_cap})

ir.name: builder_gap_threshold_pairs_001
ir.intuition: Filter to pairs with a meaningful objective gap so preferences avoid near-ties/noisy ordering and provide a cleaner training signal.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    # extra can provide a scalar gap_threshold; defaults to 0.0 (original behavior)
    gap_threshold = extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0)

    # objective shape: [B, K]; lower is better
    obj_w = objective[:, :, None]
    obj_l = objective[:, None, :]

    # winner has strictly lower objective, and gap must exceed threshold
    gap = obj_l - obj_w
    mask = (gap > gap_threshold)

    b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx = mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'gap_threshold_pairs', 'gap_threshold': gap_threshold})

ir.name: builder_anchor_gap_topk_000
ir.intuition: Build stable preferences by anchoring comparisons around per-instance best and worst candidates, and only keeping pairs with a meaningful objective gap; then cap total pairs via top-k largest gaps to respect a strict pairing budget without randomness.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    # objective: [B, K], lower is better
    B, K = objective.shape
    device = objective.device

    budget = int(extra.get('pairing_budget', extra.get('max_pairs', 128)))
    budget = max(1, budget)
    thr = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))

    # Identify best (min) and worst (max) per instance
    best_idx = objective.argmin(dim=1)  # [B]
    worst_idx = objective.argmax(dim=1)  # [B]

    # Per-instance objective gaps vs anchors
    best_val = objective.gather(1, best_idx[:, None]).squeeze(1)  # [B]
    worst_val = objective.gather(1, worst_idx[:, None]).squeeze(1)  # [B]

    diff_vs_best = objective - best_val[:, None]          # [B, K] (positive => worse than best)
    diff_worst_vs = worst_val[:, None] - objective        # [B, K] (positive => better than worst)

    # Build anchored candidate pairs: (best -> j) and (i -> worst)
    j = torch.arange(K, device=device)[None, :].expand(B, K)  # [B, K]
    b = torch.arange(B, device=device)[:, None].expand(B, K)  # [B, K]

    # best beats j if j is sufficiently worse
    mask_best = (j != best_idx[:, None]) & (diff_vs_best > thr)
    # i beats worst if i is sufficiently better
    mask_worst = (j != worst_idx[:, None]) & (diff_worst_vs > thr)

    b1 = b[mask_best]
    w1 = best_idx[:, None].expand(B, K)[mask_best]
    l1 = j[mask_best]
    s1 = diff_vs_best[mask_best]

    b2 = b[mask_worst]
    w2 = j[mask_worst]
    l2 = worst_idx[:, None].expand(B, K)[mask_worst]
    s2 = diff_worst_vs[mask_worst]

    b_idx = torch.cat([b1, b2], dim=0)
    winner_idx = torch.cat([w1, w2], dim=0)
    loser_idx = torch.cat([l1, l2], dim=0)
    score = torch.cat([s1, s2], dim=0)

    # If nothing passes the threshold, fall back to a minimal, always-valid set: best vs worst per instance
    if b_idx.numel() == 0:
        b_idx = torch.arange(B, device=device)
        winner_idx = best_idx
        loser_idx = worst_idx
        score = (worst_val - best_val)

    # Deterministic downsampling: keep the largest-gap pairs (most confident)
    if b_idx.numel() > budget:
        topk_idx = torch.topk(score, k=budget, largest=True, sorted=False).indices
        b_idx = b_idx[topk_idx]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[topk_idx]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[topk_idx]

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=None, meta={'builder': 'anchor_gap_topk', 'gap_threshold': thr, 'pairing_budget': budget})

ir.name: builder_weighted_gap_pairs_003
ir.intuition: Construct all better-vs-worse pairs from objective, but emphasize pairs with a larger objective gap and optionally drop near-ties via a configurable gap threshold; cap total pairs deterministically to a budget.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']  # [B, T]

    # Configurable thresholds/caps
    gap_thr = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))
    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 128))
    weight_scale = float(extra.get('weight_scale', 5.0))
    eps = float(extra.get('eps', 1e-6))

    # Pairwise (winner, loser) where lower objective is better.
    # gap[b,i,j] = objective[b,j] - objective[b,i] > 0 means i beats j.
    gap = objective[:, None, :] - objective[:, :, None]  # [B, T, T]
    win_mask = gap > gap_thr

    b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx = win_mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)

    # Weight pairs by (clipped) gap magnitude to emphasize clearer comparisons.
    sel_gap = gap[b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx]
    w = sel_gap / (sel_gap.detach().amax().clamp_min(eps))
    weight = (1.0 + weight_scale * w).clamp_min(0.0)

    # Deterministic cap: keep top-k by weight (no randomness).
    if b_idx.numel() > max_pairs:
        topk = torch.topk(weight, k=max_pairs, largest=True, sorted=False).indices
        b_idx = b_idx[topk]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[topk]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[topk]
        weight = weight[topk]

    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx),
        weight=weight,
        meta={
            'builder': 'weighted_gap_pairs',
            'gap_threshold': gap_thr,
            'max_pairs': max_pairs,
            'weight_scale': weight_scale,
        },
    )

ir.name: rank_stratified_band_pairs_001
ir.intuition: Builds preferences from rank bands (near-best, mid, tail) per instance: compare near-best vs tail for clear supervision, plus mid vs tail to cover harder-but-consistent improvements, using rank positions (not raw objective gaps) and per-instance caps to ensure broad coverage without enumerating all pairs.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']  # [B, N], lower is better
    B, N = objective.shape

    # Hyperparams (all deterministic)
    k_best = int(extra.get('k_best', 2))
    k_mid = int(extra.get('k_mid', 2))
    k_tail = int(extra.get('k_tail', 4))
    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 128))

    k_best = max(1, min(k_best, N))
    k_tail = max(1, min(k_tail, N))
    k_mid = max(0, min(k_mid, N))
    max_pairs = max(1, max_pairs)

    # Rank candidates by objective
    order = objective.argsort(dim=1)  # [B, N]

    # Bands
    best_idx = order[:, :k_best]  # [B, k_best]
    tail_idx = order[:, N - k_tail:]  # [B, k_tail]

    # Mid band centered around median rank (avoid overlap with best/tail when possible)
    if k_mid > 0:
        mid_center = N // 2
        start = mid_center - (k_mid // 2)
        start = max(k_best, min(start, max(k_best, N - k_tail - k_mid)))
        mid_idx = order[:, start:start + k_mid]  # [B, k_mid]
    else:
        mid_idx = order[:, :0]

    # Form pair grids within each instance (vectorized)
    # best -> tail
    w_bt = best_idx[:, :, None].expand(B, k_best, k_tail)
    l_bt = tail_idx[:, None, :].expand(B, k_best, k_tail)

    # mid -> tail
    w_mt = mid_idx[:, :, None].expand(B, k_mid, k_tail)
    l_mt = tail_idx[:, None, :].expand(B, k_mid, k_tail)

    # Flatten
    b0 = torch.arange(B, device=objective.device)[:, None]
    b_bt = b0.expand(B, k_best * k_tail).reshape(-1)
    w_bt_f = w_bt.reshape(B, k_best * k_tail).reshape(-1)
    l_bt_f = l_bt.reshape(B, k_best * k_tail).reshape(-1)

    b_mt = b0.expand(B, k_mid * k_tail).reshape(-1)
    w_mt_f = w_mt.reshape(B, k_mid * k_tail).reshape(-1)
    l_mt_f = l_mt.reshape(B, k_mid * k_tail).reshape(-1)

    b_idx = torch.cat([b_bt, b_mt], dim=0)
    winner_idx = torch.cat([w_bt_f, w_mt_f], dim=0)
    loser_idx = torch.cat([l_bt_f, l_mt_f], dim=0)

    # Remove self-pairs and any accidental non-winning comparisons (tie-safe)
    keep = winner_idx != loser_idx
    b_idx = b_idx[keep]
    winner_idx = winner_idx[keep]
    loser_idx = loser_idx[keep]

    keep2 = objective[b_idx, winner_idx] < objective[b_idx, loser_idx]
    b_idx = b_idx[keep2]
    winner_idx = winner_idx[keep2]
    loser_idx = loser_idx[keep2]

    # Per-instance cap without Python loops: take earliest pairs in a fixed construction order.
    per_inst_cap = int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_instance', k_tail * (k_best + k_mid)))
    per_inst_cap = max(1, min(per_inst_cap, k_tail * (k_best + k_mid)))

    # Reshape to [B, P] then slice per instance, then flatten back.
    P = k_tail * (k_best + k_mid)
    if P > 0:
        # Rebuild per-instance grids and slice deterministically
        w_all = torch.cat([w_bt.reshape(B, k_best * k_tail), w_mt.reshape(B, k_mid * k_tail)], dim=1)
        l_all = torch.cat([l_bt.reshape(B, k_best * k_tail), l_mt.reshape(B, k_mid * k_tail)], dim=1)
        w_all = w_all[:, :per_inst_cap]
        l_all = l_all[:, :per_inst_cap]
        b_all = torch.arange(B, device=objective.device)[:, None].expand(B, per_inst_cap)

        b_idx = b_all.reshape(-1)
        winner_idx = w_all.reshape(-1)
        loser_idx = l_all.reshape(-1)

        keep = winner_idx != loser_idx
        b_idx = b_idx[keep]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[keep]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[keep]

        keep2 = objective[b_idx, winner_idx] < objective[b_idx, loser_idx]
        b_idx = b_idx[keep2]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[keep2]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[keep2]

    # Global cap: keep largest objective improvements (deterministic)
    if b_idx.numel() > max_pairs:
        gaps = objective[b_idx, loser_idx] - objective[b_idx, winner_idx]
        _, sel = torch.topk(gaps, k=max_pairs, largest=True)
        b_idx = b_idx[sel]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[sel]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[sel]

    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx),
        weight=None,
        meta={
            'builder': 'rank_stratified_band_pairs',
            'k_best': k_best,
            'k_mid': k_mid,
            'k_tail': k_tail,
            'max_pairs': max_pairs,
            'max_pairs_per_instance': per_inst_cap,
        },
    )

ir.name: rank_quantile_adjacent_topk_noround_fix
ir.intuition: Build objective-consistent preferences by taking a few fixed rank-quantile anchor candidates (best/mid/tail by objective) and pairing each anchor against nearby ranks within a small window, then keeping the largest objective-margin pairs per instance to limit pair count while still sampling across the ranking.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']  # [B, N], lower is better
    B, N = objective.shape
    device = objective.device

    # Rank candidates per instance.
    ranks = objective.argsort(dim=1, descending=False)  # [B, N]

    # Deterministic quantile anchors in rank space.
    q_best = float(extra.get('q_best', 0.0))
    q_mid = float(extra.get('q_mid', 0.5))
    q_tail = float(extra.get('q_tail', 1.0))

    def _clamp01(x):
        if x < 0.0:
            return 0.0
        if x > 1.0:
            return 1.0
        return x

    def _q_to_r(q):
        # Map q in [0,1] to rank in [0, N-1] without using round().
        q = _clamp01(float(q))
        if N <= 1:
            return 0
        # Nearest integer via floor(x + 0.5).
        r = int(q * (N - 1) + 0.5)
        if r < 0:
            r = 0
        if r > (N - 1):
            r = N - 1
        return r

    r_best = _q_to_r(q_best)
    r_mid = _q_to_r(q_mid)
    r_tail = _q_to_r(q_tail)

    anchors_r = torch.tensor([r_best, r_mid, r_tail], device=device, dtype=torch.long)  # [A]

    # Compare each anchor to a small adjacent window of ranks.
    win = int(extra.get('adjacent_window', 4))
    if win < 1:
        win = 1
    if N > 1 and win > (N - 1):
        win = N - 1

    offsets = torch.arange(-win, win + 1, device=device, dtype=torch.long)
    offsets = offsets[offsets != 0]

    # Pair grid in rank space: [A, O]
    a_r = anchors_r[:, None].expand(anchors_r.numel(), offsets.numel())
    b_r = (a_r + offsets[None, :]).clamp(min=0, max=max(0, N - 1))

    # Map rank positions -> original indices. Advanced indexing yields [B, A*O].
    a_idx = ranks[:, a_r.reshape(-1)]
    b_idx2 = ranks[:, b_r.reshape(-1)]

    P = a_idx.shape[1]
    b = torch.arange(B, device=device)[:, None].expand(B, P)

    b_flat = b.reshape(-1)
    i_flat = a_idx.reshape(-1)
    j_flat = b_idx2.reshape(-1)

    # Drop self pairs (possible due to clamping collisions when N small).
    ns = i_flat != j_flat
    b_flat = b_flat[ns]
    i_flat = i_flat[ns]
    j_flat = j_flat[ns]

    # Orient by objective (strictly better wins).
    oi = objective[b_flat, i_flat]
    oj = objective[b_flat, j_flat]
    gap = (oj - oi)  # positive => i beats j

    pos = gap > 0
    neg = gap < 0

    b_pos = b_flat[pos]
    w_pos = i_flat[pos]
    l_pos = j_flat[pos]
    m_pos = gap[pos]

    b_neg = b_flat[neg]
    w_neg = j_flat[neg]
    l_neg = i_flat[neg]
    m_neg = (-gap[neg])

    if b_pos.numel() == 0 and b_neg.numel() == 0:
        empty = torch.empty((0,), device=device, dtype=torch.long)
        return PrefBatch(
            mode='pairwise',
            pair_idx=(empty, empty, empty),
            weight=None,
            meta={
                'builder': 'rank_quantile_adjacent_topk_noround_fix',
                'q_best': q_best,
                'q_mid': q_mid,
                'q_tail': q_tail,
                'adjacent_window': win,
            },
        )

    b_all = torch.cat([b_pos, b_neg], dim=0)
    w_all = torch.cat([w_pos, w_neg], dim=0)
    l_all = torch.cat([l_pos, l_neg], dim=0)
    margin = torch.cat([m_pos, m_neg], dim=0)

    # Optional minimum gap to avoid near-ties.
    gap_thr = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))
    keep_gap = margin > gap_thr
    b_all = b_all[keep_gap]
    w_all = w_all[keep_gap]
    l_all = l_all[keep_gap]
    margin = margin[keep_gap]

    if b_all.numel() == 0:
        empty = torch.empty((0,), device=device, dtype=torch.long)
        return PrefBatch(
            mode='pairwise',
            pair_idx=(empty, empty, empty),
            weight=None,
            meta={
                'builder': 'rank_quantile_adjacent_topk_noround_fix',
                'q_best': q_best,
                'q_mid': q_mid,
                'q_tail': q_tail,
                'adjacent_window': win,
                'gap_threshold': gap_thr,
            },
        )

    # Per-instance cap via top-k margins per instance.
    max_pairs_per_instance = int(extra.get('max_pairs_per_instance', 6))
    if max_pairs_per_instance < 1:
        max_pairs_per_instance = 1

    neg_inf = torch.full((), float('-inf'), device=device, dtype=objective.dtype)
    score = torch.full((B, N * N), neg_inf, device=device, dtype=objective.dtype)
    flat = (w_all * N + l_all).to(torch.long)
    score[b_all, flat] = margin.to(score.dtype)

    K = max_pairs_per_instance
    if K > (N * N):
        K = N * N

    topv, topi = score.topk(K, dim=1)
    keep = topv > neg_inf

    b_out = torch.arange(B, device=device)[:, None].expand(B, K)[keep].to(torch.long)
    flat_out = topi[keep].to(torch.long)
    w_out = (flat_out // N).to(torch.long)
    l_out = (flat_out % N).to(torch.long)

    # Optional global cap.
    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 0))
    if max_pairs and b_out.numel() > max_pairs:
        b_out = b_out[:max_pairs]
        w_out = w_out[:max_pairs]
        l_out = l_out[:max_pairs]

    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_out.reshape(-1).to(torch.long), w_out.reshape(-1).to(torch.long), l_out.reshape(-1).to(torch.long)),
        weight=None,
        meta={
            'builder': 'rank_quantile_adjacent_topk_noround_fix',
            'q_best': q_best,
            'q_mid': q_mid,
            'q_tail': q_tail,
            'adjacent_window': win,
            'gap_threshold': gap_thr,
            'max_pairs_per_instance': max_pairs_per_instance,
            'max_pairs': max_pairs,
        },
    )

ir.name: builder_sampled_pairs_gapweight_clip_002
ir.intuition: Keep sampled winner/loser pairs but clip the gap-based weights to a configurable max so a few extreme objective gaps don't dominate gradients, improving generalization while still downweighting near-ties.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    # Pairs where winner has lower objective (lower is better)
    mask = objective[:, :, None] < objective[:, None, :]
    b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx = mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)

    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 452))
    if b_idx.numel() > max_pairs:
        perm = torch.randperm(b_idx.numel(), device=b_idx.device)[:max_pairs]
        b_idx = b_idx[perm]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[perm]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[perm]

    # Nonnegative weighting by objective gap; optional threshold to drop near-ties
    gap = (objective[b_idx, loser_idx] - objective[b_idx, winner_idx]).clamp_min(0)
    gap_threshold = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))
    if gap_threshold > 0.0:
        keep = gap >= gap_threshold
        b_idx = b_idx[keep]
        winner_idx = winner_idx[keep]
        loser_idx = loser_idx[keep]
        gap = gap[keep]

    # Clip to avoid a few extreme gaps dominating the loss scale
    max_weight = float(extra.get('max_weight', 1.0))
    if max_weight > 0.0:
        weight = gap.clamp_max(max_weight)
    else:
        weight = gap

    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=weight, meta={'builder': 'sampled_pairs_gapweight_clip', 'max_pairs': max_pairs, 'gap_threshold': gap_threshold, 'max_weight': max_weight})

ir.name: rank_quantile_ladder_v2_fix
ir.intuition: Select a few anchor candidates at evenly spaced objective-rank quantiles per instance, then create winner/loser pairs by matching each anchor to several worse-ranked candidates at fixed positive rank offsets; this yields objective-consistent preferences with near/mid/far comparisons while avoiding O(N^2) enumeration.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    # objective: [B, N], lower is better
    B, N = objective.shape
    device = objective.device

    # Rank candidates per instance (rank 0 is best)
    ranks = objective.argsort(dim=1)

    # Choose anchor ranks as fixed quantiles
    num_anchors = int(extra.get('num_anchors', 4))
    num_anchors = max(1, min(num_anchors, N))
    if num_anchors == 1:
        anchor_r = objective.new_zeros((1,), dtype=torch.long)
    else:
        anchor_r = torch.linspace(0, N - 1, steps=num_anchors, device=device).round().to(torch.long)

    # Ladder steps in rank space (positive offsets)
    steps = extra.get('ladder_steps', None)
    if steps is None:
        s1 = 1
        s2 = 2
        s3 = max(3, (N - 1) // 2)
        step_t = torch.tensor([s1, s2, s3], device=device, dtype=torch.long)
    else:
        step_t = torch.as_tensor(steps, device=device).to(torch.long)
        if step_t.numel() == 0:
            step_t = torch.tensor([1], device=device, dtype=torch.long)
        step_t = step_t.clamp_min(1)

    A = anchor_r.numel()
    S = step_t.numel()

    # Target loser ranks per anchor: jr[a, s] = clamp(anchor_r[a] + step_t[s])
    ar = anchor_r[:, None].expand(A, S)
    jr = (ar + step_t[None, :]).clamp(max=N - 1)

    # Map rank positions to original indices
    w_idx = ranks[:, anchor_r]  # [B, A]
    l_idx = ranks[:, jr.reshape(-1)].reshape(B, A, S)  # [B, A, S]

    # Expand to flat pair lists
    w_exp = w_idx[:, :, None].expand(B, A, S)
    b_exp = torch.arange(B, device=device, dtype=torch.long)[:, None, None].expand(B, A, S)

    b_out = b_exp.reshape(-1).to(torch.long)
    w_out = w_exp.reshape(-1).to(torch.long)
    l_out = l_idx.reshape(-1).to(torch.long)

    # Remove self-pairs (can happen via clamping)
    keep = w_out != l_out
    b_out = b_out[keep]
    w_out = w_out[keep]
    l_out = l_out[keep]

    # Enforce strict objective ordering (drops ties)
    if b_out.numel() > 0:
        ow = objective[b_out, w_out]
        ol = objective[b_out, l_out]
        keep2 = ow < ol
        b_out = b_out[keep2]
        w_out = w_out[keep2]
        l_out = l_out[keep2]

    # Optional global cap (deterministic)
    max_pairs = int(extra.get('max_pairs', 0))
    if max_pairs and max_pairs > 0 and b_out.numel() > max_pairs:
        b_out = b_out[:max_pairs]
        w_out = w_out[:max_pairs]
        l_out = l_out[:max_pairs]

    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_out, w_out, l_out),
        weight=None,
        meta={
            'builder': 'rank_quantile_ladder_v2_fix',
            'num_anchors': int(num_anchors),
            'ladder_steps': step_t.tolist(),
            'max_pairs': int(max_pairs),
        },
    )

def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):

    # lower objective is better
    gap_threshold = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.05))

    # gap[b,i,j] = objective[b,j] - objective[b,i]
    # i is winner, j is loser when gap > 0

            b_idx = b_idx[keep]
            winner_idx = winner_idx[keep]
            loser_idx = loser_idx[keep]

    return PrefBatch(
        mode='pairwise',
        pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx),
        weight=None,
        meta={
            'builder': 'gap_threshold_capped_pairs',
            'gap_threshold': float(gap_threshold),

ir.name: gap_threshold_weighted_pairs
ir.intuition: Filter out near-ties by requiring an objective improvement gap, and upweight larger-gap winner/loser pairs so training focuses on clearer, more reliable preferences.
ir.code:
def generated_builder(feature_cache, extra):
    objective = feature_cache['objective']
    # Build all winner/loser pairs (lower objective is better), then drop near-ties.
    gap_threshold = float(extra.get('gap_threshold', 0.0))
    obj_w = objective[:, :, None]
    obj_l = objective[:, None, :]
    gap = obj_l - obj_w
    mask = gap > gap_threshold
    b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx = mask.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    w = gap[b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx]
    # Nonnegative weight emphasizing clearer (larger-gap) preferences.
    weight = w / (w.mean() + 1e-8)
    return PrefBatch(mode='pairwise', pair_idx=(b_idx, winner_idx, loser_idx), weight=weight, meta={'builder': 'gap_threshold_weighted_pairs', 'gap_threshold': gap_threshold})
